extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, repair stations, manufacturers, and FAA certification/inspector offices
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and compliance criteria for FAA airworthiness directives and special conditions affecting specific airplane models and equipment installations, including inspection methods, compliance times, repair/replacement options, alternate means of compliance, and documentation/contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: McDonnell Douglas DC-9 applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to Model DC-9-10, -20, -30, -40, -50, and C-9 (Military) series airplanes, fuselage numbers f through 757 and 773, certificated in any category. Compliance required as indicated, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the population of affected airplanes to which the AD applies; compliance required as indicated in the AD unless actions already accomplished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inspection: dye penetrant or eddy current per A27-288
rubrics_metrics.description: For airplanes not previously inspected in accordance with AD 87-13-04: Within 30 days after the effective date of this amendment, or in accordance with the schedule below, whichever occurs later, perform a dye penetrant or eddy current inspection of both control columns, P/N 5614272-1 and 5614272-2 for cracks, in accordance with McDonnell Douglas DC-9 Alert Service Bulletin A27-288, Revision 3, dated July 6, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection must follow McDonnell Douglas DC-9 Alert Service Bulletin A27-288, Revision 3. The AD includes an initial inspection schedule keyed to 'Accumulated landings as of July 30, 1987' with initial inspection (from July 30, 1987) landing thresholds and associated inspection values: 60,000 -> 1,500; 40,000–59,999 -> 2,000; 30,000–39,999 -> 2,500; 20,000–29,999 -> 3,000; under 20,000 -> 3,800 (landings). (July 30, 1987 is the effective date of AD 87-13-04.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive inspections interval
rubrics_metrics.description: For all airplanes: If no cracks are found, accomplish repetitive inspections in accordance with paragraph A at intervals not to exceed 3,800 landings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If airplanes were previously inspected under AD 87-13-04, the first repetitive inspection required by this paragraph must be performed within 3,800 landings after the last inspection performed in accordance with AD 87-13-04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crack disposition option 1 — blend out to 0.030 inch
rubrics_metrics.description: If crack(s) are found in either control column, one option before further flight is to blend out the cracks up to depths of 0.030 inch, maintaining minimum thickness at the specific inspection area in accordance with Table I of McDonnell Douglas DC-9 Alert Service Bulletin A27-288, using an ultrasonic method, and continually inspect at intervals not exceeding 3,800 landings, until terminating procedures are accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cracks are found after blending, or if a crack(s) is found on any previously blended column, replace the control column with a new production control column (specified P/Ns). Continued ultrasonic inspections at ≤3,800 landing intervals are required until terminating action is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crack disposition option 2 — replace per Service Bulletin 27-286
rubrics_metrics.description: If crack(s) are found, an alternative before further flight is to remove the cracked control column, P/N 5614272-1 (Captain’s) or 5614272-2 (First Officer’s), and replace it with a new production control column (specified P/Ns) in accordance with McDonnell Douglas Service Bulletin 27-286, dated May 18, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement per the specified service bulletin is an approved compliance option to address detected cracks prior to further flight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crack disposition option 3 — FAA-approved repair
rubrics_metrics.description: If crack(s) are found, an alternative is to repair in a manner approved by the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any repair used as compliance must be specifically approved by the named FAA manager (AMOC process described elsewhere in the AD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating action — replacement with new production columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement of the Captain’s and First Officer’s control column, P/N’s 5614272-1 and 5614272-2, with new control columns, P/N’s 5614272-501, -503, SB 09270286-3, and 5614272-502, -504, SB 09270288-4, respectively, constitutes terminating action for the requirements of this amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the specified replacement is accomplished, the inspection/repair requirements of this AD are terminated for that airplane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance (AMOC) — McDonnell Douglas AD
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment and then send it to the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service documents and examination locations (McDonnell Douglas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons affected who have not already received appropriate service documents may obtain copies from McDonnell Douglas Corporation (address) and may examine documents at FAA Northwest Mountain Region Transport Airplane Directorate or Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD also states it supersedes Amendment 39-5656, AD 87-13-04, and provides the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fokker Model F-28 applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to Model F-28 Mark 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000 series airplanes, certificated in any category. Compliance is required as indicated, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the affected airplane models for the Fokker AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate Fokker Structural Inspection Program (SIP) into maintenance program
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months after the effective date of this AD, incorporate into the FAA‑approved maintenance program the inspections, inspection intervals, repairs or replacements defined in the Fokker Structural Inspection Program (SIP) Document No. 28438, Part I, including revisions up through November 1, 1988; and inspect, repair, and replace, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The non‑destructive inspection techniques referenced in this document provide acceptable methods for accomplishing the inspections required by this AD. Inspection results where a crack is detected must be reported to Fokker in accordance with the instructions of the SIP document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair cracked structure prior to further flight (Fokker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cracked structure detected during the inspections required must be repaired or replaced prior to further flight, in accordance with the instructions in SIP Document No. 28438, revised November 1, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repairs must follow the SIP instructions to ensure continued structural integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance (Fokker)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Standardization Branch, ANM-113, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment and then send it to the Manager, Standardization Branch, ANM-113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits to comply (Fokker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited operation to a maintenance base to accomplish mandated actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honeywell AH-600 applicability (AHRU part/serial limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to Honeywell AH-600 AHRS Strapdown Attitude and Heading Reference Unit (AHRU), part numbers 7003360-931 through -936, with serial numbers 0100 through 0277 (serial numbers referred to in this AD are the last four numbers). Compliance required as indicated, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the specific units (part and serial numbers) and notes serial number format; known installations listed but AD not limited to those airplane makes/models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot (Number 1) AHRS inspection and removal requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after January 9, 1989 inspect airplanes with Honeywell AH-600 AHRS installed to determine the part number, serial number, and Mod Level of the strapdown AHRU installed in the pilot’s (Number 1) AHRS. Prior to further flight after inspection, remove all AHRU part numbers 7003360-931 through -936 with serial numbers 0100 through 0277, without Mod Level 'F', from service in the pilot’s (Number 1) AHRS. Install the same part number with Mod Level 'F' incorporated, or modify the AHRU in accordance with Honeywell Service Bulletin 7003360-34-32, dated August 2, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is immediate pilot-side mitigation: removal or modification must be done before further flight when affected units are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copilot (Number 2) and auxiliary (Number 3) AHRS inspection/removal schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 calendar days after the effective date, inspect copilot’s (Number 2) and auxiliary (Number 3) AHRS to determine the part number, serial number, and Mod Level. Within 45 days after the inspection, remove all AHRU part numbers 7003360-931 through -936 with serial numbers 0100 through 0277, without Mod Level 'F', from service in the copilot’s and auxiliary AHRS, and install the same part number with Mod Level 'F' or modify in accordance with Honeywell Service Bulletin 7003360-34-32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides staged inspection and compliance timing for non‑pilot systems to mitigate dual-failure risk fleetwide while considering parts availability and maintenance scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC and special flight permits (Honeywell AD)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time may be used when approved by the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office; special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMOC requests should be forwarded through an FAA PMI who will concur or comment before sending to the Manager; permits allow limited ferry flights to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: GROB Werke applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to GROB WERKE GmbH & Co KG Model TWIN ASTIR, TWIN ASTIR TRAINER, G103 TWIN II, and G103A TWIN II ACRO gliders for specified serial number ranges, certificated in any category. Compliance required as indicated, unless already accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the affected glider models and serial number ranges for which the AD is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultrasonic inspection of end spar spigots within 500 takeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the next 500 takeoffs after the effective date of this AD, inspect the wing spar spigots for damage in accordance with the ultrasonic inspection procedures specified in GROB WERKE Technical Information TM 315-36, dated June 23, 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection method and service document are specified; timeliness requirement is strict (within 500 takeoffs).

rubrics_metrics.name: If damage found—remove and replace prior to further flight
rubrics_metrics.description: If damage is found, prior to further flight remove and replace the spigot with a Fail-Safe Spigot using the procedures specified in the referenced service information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damage disposition requires immediate replacement with an approved Fail‑Safe Spigot following the manufacturer's procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no damage—replace with Fail‑Safe Spigots within 500 takeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: If no damage is found, within the next 500 takeoffs remove and replace the spigots with Fail‑Safe Spigots using the procedures specified in the referenced service information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD mandates proactive replacement with Fail‑Safe spigots regardless of inspection findings within a specified interval to preclude future failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement considered major airframe repair—FAA repair station requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The replacement of the wing spigots is considered major airframe repair and must be accomplished at FAA certified repair stations rated for composite construction of small aircraft, using Grob Werke repair methods for the model of interest, approved by the FAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes Type Certificate Data Sheet guidance and limits who may perform the replacement (FAA-certified composite repair stations) and the need to use approved methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC (GROB AD)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance or adjustment of the compliance times which provides an equivalent level of safety may be approved by the Manager, Brussels Aircraft Certification Staff, FAA (c/o American Embassy, Brussels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be forwarded through an FAA Maintenance Inspector, who may add comments and send it to the Manager, Brussels Aircraft Certification Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special conditions applicability for Beech Model 55 EFIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions are issued for incorporation of an electronic flight instrument system (EFIS) in the Beech Model 55 Series Airplanes because the proposed EFIS installation has novel and unusual design features not envisaged by existing airworthiness standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special conditions become part of the type certification basis for the airplane and will apply to similar EFIS installations without further amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of EFIS from High Energy Radiated Fields (HERF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic displays and their installation must include protection from high energy radiated electromagnetic fields (HERF) for which the applicable regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate airworthiness standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special conditions provide additional safety standards necessary to establish an equivalent level of safety to existing airworthiness standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display legibility in all cockpit lighting conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissive color on a CRT display will appear different than reflective colors and ambient illumination affects perceived colors; therefore, display legibility must be adequate for all cockpit lighting conditions including direct sunlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility requirement covers different intensities/color temperatures and extreme lighting (direct sunlight) to ensure pilot can read critical flight information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective reliability requirement for electronic displays replacing traditional instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: For installations where electronic displays take the place of traditional instruments, the reliability must not be less than that of the traditional instruments; this concerns the collective reliability of the traditional instruments rather than the reliability of a single traditional instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifying the EFIS requires demonstrating at least the same overall capability/reliability afforded by the set of traditional instruments it replaces (not merely parity with one instrument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design requirements when a single malfunction may affect multiple instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions provide requirements for installations featuring design characteristics where a single malfunction or failure could affect more than one primary instrument, display, or system; requirements assure adequate reliability of system design functions essential for continued safe flight and landing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because modern EFIS can present multiple flight functions on a common display, the special conditions address redundancy, failure modes, and reliability to prevent a single fault from compromising essential flight information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flight instrument placement/grouping consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Flight instruments for the pilot are required to be grouped in front of the pilot so deviation from looking forward along the airplane flight path is minimized when the pilot shifts from viewing the flight path to viewing the flight instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This human‑factors/layout principle is reiterated as relevant when replacing traditional instruments with electronic displays, to preserve pilot scan and minimal head/eye movement.
